chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who delegated the affair of his wife to a man, so he said, 'Bear witness that I have delegated the affair of so-and-so to so-and-so.' Is that permissible for the man? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to delegate the authority of divorce to another person?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith validates the legal concept of *Tafwid* (delegation), where a husband explicitly authorizes a third party to execute a divorce. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital contracts, allowing for the transfer of specific rights to ensure procedural clarity and mutual consent.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, altogether from Safwan Bin yahya, from Saeed Al A’araj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who made the matter of his wife to a man, so he said, ‘Bear witness that I made the matter of so and so woman to so and so man’. Is that allowed for the man?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz from Ayyub ibn Nuh Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Sa‘id al-A’raj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has left the affair of his wife to another man saying, ‘Bear witness that I have left the affairs of so and so, to so and so; if it is permissible for the man. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is permissible.’ ”
